extracted.intended_audience: regulatory stakeholders, federal agencies, industry cybersecurity practitioners, legal/regulatory researchers, and public commenters tracking federal cybersecurity rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register search-results listing of documents matching the term "cybersecurity," aggregating notices, proposed and final rules, guidance availability, information-collection requests, and meeting notices across multiple federal agencies. Useful for finding regulatory requirements, program criteria, and publication excerpts related to federal cybersecurity policy and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of a Cybersecurity Coordinator
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection concerns data concerning the designation of a Cybersecurity Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears as an information-collection element (TSA ICR) — organizations are expected to identify and record who serves as the Cybersecurity Coordinator for the covered entity as part of compliance/ICR reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of cybersecurity incidents to CISA
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection concerns the reporting of cybersecurity incidents to the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities subject to the collection/requirement must report cybersecurity incidents to CISA in the manner and timeframe specified by the applicable rule or information-collection instrument (cited across TSA and other notices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a cybersecurity contingency/recovery plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection concerns the development of a cybersecurity contingency/recovery plan to address cybersecurity gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies expect covered entities to develop contingency and recovery plans that identify cybersecurity gaps and define steps to recover operations; this is an explicit ICR element and often tied to plan documentation and assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of a cybersecurity assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection concerns the completion of a cybersecurity assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities must complete and provide evidence of cybersecurity assessments as part of information collections or program compliance (e.g., TSA ICR). Guidance on scope/method is provided in the underlying rule or guidance document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum cybersecurity requirements for marine transportation entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish minimum cybersecurity requirements for U.S.-flagged vessels, Outer Continental Shelf facilities, and MTSA-regulated facilities including requirements to develop and maintain a Cybersecurity Plan, designate a Cybersecurity Officer, and take measures to maintain cybersecurity within the marine transportation system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final Coast Guard rule requires covered maritime entities to maintain a Cybersecurity Plan, designate a Cybersecurity Officer, and implement measures to detect risks and to respond to and recover from cybersecurity incidents; implementation periods and potential delays may be subject to comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cybersecurity Performance Goals (CPGs) as baseline practices
rubrics_metrics.description: CISA's Cybersecurity Performance Goals (CPGs) are baseline practices that critical infrastructure entities can use to manage and reduce cybersecurity risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CPGs are sector-agnostic, prioritized guidance; agencies reference them as voluntary baseline practices and provide assessment training and tools to support adoption. Use CPGs to focus resources on high-impact risk-reduction measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: IoT Cybersecurity Labeling program requirements (FCC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a voluntary cybersecurity labeling program for wireless consumer IoT products providing an FCC IoT Label that includes the U.S. Cyber Trust Mark and a QR code linked to a dynamic, decentralized, publicly available registry of more detailed cybersecurity information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program goals: help consumers make safer purchasing decisions and encourage security-by-design. Specific developer capabilities required include the ability to receive information relevant to cybersecurity and respond to customer queries; provide up-to-date registry information accessible via QR code; meet 'cybersecurity utility' and information-dissemination expectations described in the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information and Query Reception for IoT developers
rubrics_metrics.description: The IoT product developer has the ability to receive information relevant to cybersecurity and respond to queries from the customer and others about information relevant to cybersecurity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labeling program expects product developers to maintain channels/processes to accept reports and queries, and to use customer reports to improve IoT product cybersecurity over time ('cybersecurity utility').

rubrics_metrics.name: Align acquisition workforce descriptions with the NICE Framework
rubrics_metrics.description: When acquiring IT support services or cybersecurity support services, agencies should describe the cybersecurity workforce tasks, knowledge, skills, and work roles to align with the NICE Framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAR proposed amendments require contract descriptions of workforce qualifications to use the common language/categories in the NICE Framework so that solicitations specify required competencies and work roles consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA premarket cybersecurity content for medical devices
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA recommends information to industry regarding cybersecurity device design, labeling, and the documentation that FDA recommends be included in premarket submissions for devices with cybersecurity risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final FDA guidance (updated) identifies what documentation the FDA generally considers necessary to support cybersecurity-related obligations under the FD&C Act amendments; includes quality system considerations and content expectations for premarket submissions (design, labeling, testing, risk assessments, mitigations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant and project criteria for Schools and Libraries Cybersecurity Pilot
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications should describe the cybersecurity risks the proposed Pilot project will prevent or address; the cybersecurity equipment and services the applicant plans to request; the ability of the project to be self-sustaining; whether the applicant has a cybersecurity officer or senior-level staff designated for the Pilot; and previous experience implementing cybersecurity protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FCC Pilot program evaluative criteria focus on risk addressed, planned services/equipment, sustainability after funding, presence of designated cybersecurity leadership, and prior implementation experience — applicants should document each element in their proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMMC Program verification and maintenance of status
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD will verify contractors have implemented required security measures necessary to safeguard Federal Contract Information (FCI) and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and will confirm a contractor's CMMC level and assessment type is maintained across the contract period of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CMMC Program establishes levels and assessment mechanisms; DoD will use rulemaking updates as needed to adapt to evolving standards and threats. Contractors must attain and maintain required CMMC level (and provide evidence/UIDs) for contract eligibility and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: DFARS/Contract clause definitions and obligations (CUI, CMMC, POA&M, UID)
rubrics_metrics.description: DFARS provisions define terms such as controlled unclassified information (CUI), Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) status, CMMC unique identifier (CMMC UID), Federal contract information (FCI), and Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M), and incorporate contractual cybersecurity requirements tied to CMMC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicitations and contracts will include clauses (e.g., DFARS 252.204-7021) that require contractor compliance with CMMC-level requirements, reporting of POA&Ms, and maintenance of identifiers/status as defined in the DFARS text.

rubrics_metrics.name: HIPAA Security Rule modifications to strengthen ePHI cybersecurity
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revisions to the HIPAA Security Rule to better protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of electronic protected health information (ePHI), addressing changes in care environments, increases in breaches/cyberattacks, common compliance deficiencies, and relevant best practices and court decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS proposes specific modifications to standards and implementation specifications to increase protections for ePHI; regulated entities should anticipate updated requirements and align security practices (technical/administrative/physical) accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for Department of Defense University Consortium Support Center
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for the UC2 Support Center, institutions must have been designated as National Centers of Academic Excellence (NCAE) in cybersecurity for at least 24 months, demonstrate an understanding of cybersecurity research, be eligible for access to classified material, and demonstrate commitment to the UC2 mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must document NCAE designation duration, research capability, security eligibility, and institutional commitments to collaboration with DoD; selection is tied to meeting these explicit eligibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information collection requirements: OMB control numbers, burden estimates, and electronic submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency information-collection notices include OMB control numbers, estimated burdens (time, respondents, responses), frequency, affected public, and may permit or encourage electronic submissions of responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When responding to or complying with federal ICRs, entities should follow the specified OMB control number, provide data consistent with the burden estimates, and use permitted automated/electronic submission methods where allowed.
